issues.description: Seen now carries two overlapping fields (ref, parent) with implicit coupling rules
issues.detail: The data structure grew a second pointer (parent) alongside ref, and the relationship between them is encoded in conditional logic spread across process() and finalize() (e.g. 'if (!result.ref) result.ref = parent', 'isParentRef = parent === ref', 'seen.parent && seen.parent !== ref'). Two fields that sometimes alias, sometimes diverge, and whose semantics depend on whether a processor ran first — that is the wrong data structure. A single discriminated field (e.g. inheritFrom with a tag: 'processor' | 'parent' | 'both') would make the algorithm in finalize self-evident instead of requiring three separate branches that re-derive intent.

issues.description: Property de-duplication by JSON.stringify equality is too clever for what it is
issues.detail: Two separate loops in finalize delete keys from the child schema when JSON.stringify(child[key]) === JSON.stringify(parent[key]). Stringify-compare-and-delete is a structural-equality hack that allocates strings on every key of every schema, will mis-handle key ordering inside nested objects, and silently does nothing when equality 'almost' holds. The data shape (child overrides vs inherited props) should be tracked at assignment time — record which keys came from _cached vs from refSchema — so the dedupe step is a set-difference, not a stringify comparison.

issues.description: flattenRef now does three jobs; it should be one stateless transform
issues.detail: flattenRef merges ref properties, then conditionally strips parent-only keys, then separately walks seen.parent to propagate $ref and dedupe again. That is three passes glued together with mutation of the shared schema object and recursive re-entry guarded by 'seen.ref = null'. A cleaner shape: one pass that computes the final JSON node from (own props, inherited props, parent $ref) as inputs and returns it. Right now the function reads as a sequence of patches whose correctness depends on order, which is exactly the situation Rule 5 warns about — the data dominates and the data isn't organized.

issues.description: Override count doubled from 6 to 12 with no explanation in the test or commit
issues.detail: The assertion went from toBe(6) to toBe(12) with the only context being the new parent-tracking. Doubling the number of override invocations is a real behavior change — overrides may now run on both child and parent nodes in the clone chain. That deserves either a comment in the test explaining why 12 is correct, or a guard so overrides don't double-fire on parents that are effectively the same logical schema. Quietly updating the magic number hides a semantic shift from future readers.

issues.description: play.ts and a stray commented line look like leftover scratch
issues.detail: play.ts was rewritten into a debug script importing from a relative source path, and mini/schemas.ts removes a '// { parent: true }' comment by uncommenting it — fine, but the diff still reads like in-flight work. play.ts should not ship as part of a feature PR, and the comment-to-code transition deserves a one-line note that this was intentionally enabled to match classic. Small hygiene, not load-bearing.

issues.description: fileProcessor change is good but the test snapshot loses validation properties from anyOf branches
issues.detail: Moving shared props (contentEncoding, format, maxLength, minLength, type) to the root and leaving only contentMediaType in each anyOf branch is the right composition — exactly the 'factor out what's common' move. Worth noting that consumers reading only one anyOf branch in isolation will no longer see the string constraints; for JSON Schema validators this is fine (anyOf merges with siblings), but downstream tooling that walks anyOf naively may regress. A one-line comment in fileProcessor explaining the merge semantics would prevent the next person from undoing it.

review.summary: The fix works and the intent is right: track parent separately from processor-ref so $ref propagation survives wrapper chains. But the data structure grew a second pointer without grooming, and finalize() now reads as three patches over a shared mutable schema object, dedup'd by JSON.stringify equality. Data dominates here — and the data (Seen) is doing two jobs that should be one. The fileProcessor refactor is a clean composition win. Recommend: unify ref/parent into a single inheritance descriptor, track which keys are owned vs inherited at assignment time so the dedupe step becomes set-difference instead of stringify-compare, and explain the 6→12 override-count change in the test before merging.
